preconditions.description: The number of stations (and passages) is an integer between 3 and 3000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n and 1 <= int(y) <= n and int(x) != int(y) for x, y in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
preconditions.description: Each passage connects two distinct stations numbered from 1 to n, inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len({(min(int(x), int(y)), max(int(x), int(y))) for x, y in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])}) == n
preconditions.description: There are exactly n unique passages, each connecting a unique pair of stations (no duplicates).

preconditions.expression: all(any((int(x) == a and int(y) == b) or (int(x) == b and int(y) == a) for x, y in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])) for a, b in {(min(int(x), int(y)), max(int(x), int(y))) for x, y in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])})
preconditions.description: The input represents a connected undirected graph (classic subway scheme).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() == ['0' if station in ringroad else str(min_distance) for station in range(1, n + 1)]
postconditions.description: For each station, the output is its distance to the ringroad (0 if it is part of the ringroad). The distance is the minimum number of passages required to reach any station on the ringroad.

postconditions.expression: len(ringroad) >= 3 and all((ringroad[i] != ringroad[j] for i in range(len(ringroad)) if i != j) for j in range(len(ringroad)))
postconditions.description: The ringroad is a cycle of at least 3 distinct stations, where each consecutive pair (and the first/last pair) is connected by a passage.

postconditions.expression: all(any((ringroad[i] == station and ringroad[(i + 1) % len(ringroad)] == neighbor) or (ringroad[i] == neighbor and ringroad[(i + 1) % len(ringroad)] == station) for i in range(len(ringroad))) for station, neighbor in {(min(int(x), int(y)), max(int(x), int(y))) for x, y in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])})
postconditions.description: The ringroad is a Hamiltonian cycle in the graph (uses exactly n passages and all stations).

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(distance) <= n - 1 for distance in stdout.strip().split())
postconditions.description: Each station's distance to the ringroad is a non-negative integer not exceeding n - 1.
